takeaway: Portosystemic anastomoses: lower oesophagus, anal canal, umbilicus, retroperitoneum, bare area of liver. The superior and inferior pancreaticoduodenal veins are both portal, so they are not a site.

question.text: Which of the following is not a site for communication between the portal and systemic venous systems?

answer.text: Between the superior and inferior pancreaticoduodenal veins
answer.say: Between the superior and inferior pancreatico-duodenal veins

lines.text: Portal blood has a few places to meet the systemic veins.
At the lower oesophagus, the left gastric branches join the azygos vein.
At the anal canal, the superior rectal vein joins the middle and inferior rectal veins.
Around the umbilicus, paraumbilical veins meet the epigastric veins, giving caput medusae.
lines.say: Around the umbilicus, paraumbilical veins meet the epigastric veins, giving caput medusae. (sigh)

lines.text: In the retroperitoneum, portal tributaries meet the lumbar and renal veins.
But the superior and inferior pancreaticoduodenal veins are both portal.
lines.say: But the superior and inferior pancreatico-duodenal veins are both portal.

lines.text: Two portal veins shaking hands is no link to the systemic system, so this is not a portosystemic site.
